answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every identity must post a refundable stake before it can earn: a newcomer is a low-trust vertex in the trust graph, allowed only tiny jobs, and each completed attestation adds weight. A fake that spawns a thousand clones must fund a thousand stakes, while the nectar of real work - verified deliveries - flows only to vertices with a long, costly history. Cheating triggers slashing of the stake, so creating identities costs more than any single fraud can repay.
